blocks.text: All organisms use the same basic mechanism of reading and expressing genes, which is often referred to as central dogma. The first step of central dogma is the transfer of information from DNA to RNA, which occurs when an RNA copy of the gene is produced. The process is called transcription. The second step of the central dogma is the transfer of information from RNA to proteins, which occurs when the information contained in the RNA is used to direct the synthesis of proteins. This process is called translation. In this way DNA controls the properties and activities of a cell.
